scope: Factual, public-source metadata taxonomy spanning geological deep time, prehistory, antiquity, historical periods, and the modern digital era.
important_definition: Metadata is data describing an object, record, dataset, event, system, specimen, observation, or digital artifact. There is no single dataset containing everything.

neural_metadata_boundary.definition: Observable or recorded information about nervous-system activity, neural measurements, experimental conditions, or computational neural-network systems.
neural_metadata_boundary.not_included: Private or inferred thoughts, mental states, identities, or other information that is not actually measured or publicly documented. Neural activity cannot be reconstructed as factual metadata merely from a person's name, behavior, or ordinary digital activity.

quality_rules: Do not present inference as observation
Do not treat metadata as the underlying content
Distinguish primary evidence from later interpretation
Record source provenance and retrieval dates
Do not infer private neural activity from public behavior
Do not fabricate missing historical records
Mark disputed claims and competing interpretations explicitly
Preserve revisions rather than silently overwriting historical values
coverage_limitations: No universal all-time metadata corpus exists
Ancient and prehistoric evidence is incomplete and preservation-biased
Some modern data is private or access-controlled
Some datasets are restricted for privacy, security, legal, ownership, or preservation reasons
A factual inventory can only represent sources that actually exist and are accessible
privacy_security_boundary: no credentials, tokens, or private keys
no private medical or financial records
no classified material obtained through unauthorized means
no destructive scientific or archaeological probing
status: Factual all-time metadata taxonomy added to Prev_NW.
